title: Private minimum pack: GPU saturation, OOM, restart-loop, and resource pressure alert rules
creator: Allison Grant
description:
Context
Private installs need a supported baseline set of alerts that catch the highest-impact inference failure modes without causing alert storms in customer clusters. This ticket covers GPU saturation, GPU memory pressure, OOM kills, restart loops, and related resource pressure signals for the serving runtime pods.

Scope
- Prometheus alert rules (and any required recording rules) for:
  1) GPU saturation (sustained high utilization / throttling symptoms)
  2) GPU memory pressure (near-full VRAM) that precedes OOM kills
  3) OOM kills (container OOMKilled) and GPU-related crash signatures where available
  4) Restart loops for runtime pods (CrashLoopBackOff / high restart rate)
  5) Kubernetes node/pod resource pressure that commonly manifests as inference flakiness (memory pressure / eviction signals where feasible)
- Alerts must be compatible with the Private minimum pack constraints:
  - bounded label cardinality (avoid per-request / per-tenant / per-route)
  - works in air-gapped installs (no external dependencies)
  - safe defaults: page only for high-confidence, high-blast-radius issues; otherwise create tickets
  - embed “what to do first” + runbook links in alert annotations

Non-goals (v1)
- Per-model or per-tenant GPU hot-spot alerts (too high-cardinality for Private defaults)
- Advanced GPU health telemetry (ECC error deep dives, per-SM metrics) unless already exported by the supported GPU exporter

Implementation details / proposed rule set
Exporter assumptions:
- Supported baseline is NVIDIA DCGM exporter if enabled by customer (common in VPC/on-prem).
- Where DCGM metrics are unavailable, fall back to Kubernetes-level symptoms (OOMKilled, restarts) and Redwood runtime-exported process metrics.

Rule naming + grouping
- Group: redwood_private_runtime_gpu
- Prefix: RedwoodPrivateRuntime*
- Labels: severity, component=runtime, product=private, signal=gpu|k8s
- Required routing labels (consistent with standards doc): severity, team (SRE vs Private Deployments), service

Alerts (final set shipped in v1)
1) RedwoodPrivateRuntimeGPUUtilizationSustainedHigh
- Intent: detect fleet-level saturation that will cause queueing/latency/SLO burn.
- Expression (DCGM): avg by (namespace, deployment) (DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL) > 95 for 15m
- Severity: sev2 (page) only when affecting >= N pods (see tuning), otherwise sev3 (ticket)
- Notes: This is intentionally conservative; high util is expected, but sustained 95%+ across replicas correlates with queuing and tail latency increases.

2) RedwoodPrivateRuntimeGPUMemoryNearFull
- Intent: early warning for imminent OOM / allocator failures.
- Expression (DCGM): (avg by (namespace, deployment) (DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED) / avg by (namespace, deployment) (DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_TOTAL)) > 0.92 for 10m
- Severity: sev3 (ticket)
- Action: scale replicas / reduce max_batch_tokens / verify KV cache limits and model footprint.

3) RedwoodPrivateRuntimeContainerOOMKilled
- Intent: explicit signal that runtime containers are being OOMKilled by kubelet.
- Expression (kube-state-metrics): sum by (namespace, pod, container) (increase(kube_pod_container_status_last_terminated_reason{reason="OOMKilled"}[15m])) > 0
- Severity: sev2 (page) if count across pods >= 3 in 15m; else sev3
- Notes: Avoids relying on log parsing; works in most customer clusters.

4) RedwoodPrivateRuntimeHighRestartRate
- Intent: restart loop / flapping runtime pods.
- Expression: sum by (namespace, pod, container) (increase(kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total[10m])) >= 3
- Severity: sev2 (page) if >= 2 pods in same deployment affected; else sev3
- Notes: Pairs well with OOMKilled, image pull, or config issues. Runbook instructs checking events and last termination reason first.

5) RedwoodPrivateRuntimeCrashLoopBackOff
- Intent: catch steady-state CrashLoopBackOff before it cascades.
- Expression: max by (namespace, pod, container) (kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{reason="CrashLoopBackOff"}) > 0 for 10m
- Severity: sev2 (page)

6) RedwoodPrivateRuntimeNodeMemoryPressureAffectingRuntime (optional / disabled by default)
- Intent: node pressure that may evict runtime pods or cause kernel OOM.
- Expression: max by (node) (kube_node_status_condition{condition="MemoryPressure",status="true"}) > 0
- Severity: sev3 (ticket)
- Default: OFF in values.yaml to reduce noise for smaller clusters; documented as opt-in.

Cardinality / label constraints
- No alerts keyed on model, route, or tenant.
- Aggregations are by (namespace, deployment) or (namespace, pod) only.
- If deployment label not available, use (namespace, app) per Helm chart label conventions.

Annotations requirements (per oncall feedback)
- Each alert includes:
  - summary: one line
  - impact: what breaks for inference
  - runbook_url: Confluence runbook section anchor
  - first_steps: 2–4 bullet actions (kubectl describe pod, check OOMKilled, check GPU mem, check recent config/rollout)
  - escalation: when to page Redwood Support/SRE vs customer platform team

Acceptance criteria
- Rules included in the observability-pack bundle and wired into private Helm values.
- Rules render and evaluate cleanly in the private smoke-test harness.
- Noise review completed with SRE (at least one staging private cluster run >= 72 hours) and thresholds adjusted.
- Runbook links included and valid.
- Defaults match alert severity taxonomy for Private: page only for high-confidence, high-impact, multi-replica issues.

Testing plan
- Staging private cluster (VPC-like) failure injection:
  - force GPU saturation by constraining replicas and sending load; verify Utilization alert triggers only when sustained.
  - induce VRAM pressure (larger context / concurrency) to trigger GPUMemoryNearFull.
  - induce OOMKilled by setting low memory limit in canary runtime deployment.
  - force CrashLoopBackOff via bad env var / config to validate waiting_reason alert.
- Verify annotations include runbook_url and first_steps.

Rollout plan
- Ship alerts enabled by default except NodeMemoryPressure (off by default).
- Document tuning knobs in values.yaml (thresholds, minimum affected pods, enable/disable per rule group).
- Backport to the private-2025.08 release branch per release coordination.
comments: 2025-06-11 — Allison Grant: Creating this ticket as part of minimum pack alerting tranche. Please keep to the private standards doc (severity mapping + cardinality caps). Coordinate with Aisha on paging vs ticket thresholds.
2025-06-13 — Sergio Costa: Drafting rule set in observability-pack. Plan is DCGM-based util/mem + kube-state-metrics for OOMKilled/restarts. Will keep aggregations to namespace/deployment only.

2025-06-17 — Thomas Baird: Reminder: avoid gpu_uuid labels; DCGM defaults include uuid sometimes depending on exporter config. Please ensure rules don’t group by uuid/device unless explicitly required. If unavoidable, drop labels via relabel_configs in the packaged scrape config.

2025-06-21 — Rafael Mendes: Strong preference to page only when multiple pods affected. Single pod OOMKill is often a noisy symptom during rollouts. Recommend sev2 paging only when >=2 pods in same deployment restart-loop within 10m or OOMKilled >=3 within 15m.

2025-06-26 — Sergio Costa: Implemented thresholds per SRE guidance. Added first_steps annotations (kubectl describe pod, check termination reason/events, check GPU mem panel, check last rollout). Open question: do we ship NodeMemoryPressure enabled by default? Leaning off-by-default.

2025-07-01 — Aisha Bello: +1 off-by-default for node pressure in v1. Keep it documented as opt-in; too much variance across customer clusters. Ensure alert titles clearly indicate ‘customer cluster condition’ vs ‘Redwood runtime symptom’.
2025-07-08 — Sergio Costa: PR up with alerts + recording rules where needed. Added runbook_url placeholders pointing to Private day-2 runbook sections; Elliot/Kira to confirm final anchors.

2025-07-15 — Rafael Mendes: Ran in staging private cluster for 4 days; no pages; sev3 tickets matched expected load tests. Adjusted GPUMemoryNearFull from 90% to 92% to reduce false positives during batch spikes.

2025-08-07 — Sergio Costa: Merged in observability-pack PR-18372. Follow-up: ensure Helm wiring defaults match (ENG-19152) and smoke tests updated (ENG-19156). Marking done for rule authoring + noise review.
